questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes KV caching from caching one fixed next-token distribution?

options.A: KV caching forces every generation step to reuse identical output probabilities.
options.B: KV caching stores only the most probable vocabulary token at each position.
options.C: KV caching reuses prefix representations while each new query computes updated attention and output probabilities.
options.D: KV caching removes the need to process any newly generated token.

questions.explanation: Cached prefix keys and values are reused, but the newly processed token supplies new queries and produces updated attention outputs and next-token probabilities.
